title: Mandäische Liturgien (German, Lidzbarski 1920)
author: Mark Lidzbarski
description: Mandäische Liturgien (Mandaean Liturgies), edited and translated into German by Mark Lidzbarski (Berlin: Weidmann, 1920, Abhandlungen der Königlichen Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen). It contains the Mandaic text, transliterated, of the main liturgical collections of the Mandaeans, the Gnostic baptist community of Iraq and Iran, with a German translation. The core is the Qolasta, the canonical prayer book with hymns and prayers for baptism (masbuta), the 'ascent of the soul' or death mass (masiqta), and daily prayers, together with the Oxford collection of liturgies. The hymns praise the Great Life and the beings of light, invoke the living water and seek the soul's safe return through the watch-houses to the world of light. With his translations of the Ginza and the Book of John, this completes Lidzbarski's great trilogy that founded modern Mandaean studies.
